title: Where does each number sit in the grid?
description: Numbers fill an endless grid of four columns. The number in row r and column c is four times the bracket r minus one, plus c, and this gives the row and column of one hundred and twenty four, one hundred and forty seven and two hundred and one.
teaching_notes: One idea: each full row holds four numbers, so row r starts after r minus one full rows. Watch for students who forget that a remainder of zero means column four.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the bracket formula: the full rows before are counted with a bracket, and the position in the row is added.
video_script.substitution: The method of three plus two times the bracket y minus one, with four times the bracket r minus one plus c for the grid.
video_script.anchor: an endless grid of four columns filled with numbers in order
video_script.payoff_line: Row r and column c hold four times the bracket r minus one, plus c

final_answer.value: (a) 4(r − 1) + c for column c (b) 124 at row 31 column 4, 147 at row 37 column 3, 201 at row 51 column 1 (c) 4(r − 1) + c (d) multiples of 3 follow the columns 3, 2, 1, 4 repeating; column 4 holds multiples of 4; even numbers sit in columns 2 and 4; odd numbers in columns 1 and 3
final_answer.spoken: row r and column c hold four times the bracket r minus one, plus c

hold_back: Answer: (a) 4(r − 1) + c for column c (b) 124 at row 31 column 4, 147 at row 37 column 3, 201 at row 51 column 1 (c) 4(r − 1) + c (d) multiples of 3 follow the columns 3, 2, 1, 4 repeating; column 4 holds multiples of 4; even numbers sit in columns 2 and 4; odd numbers in columns 1 and 3
never_show: the finished formula before the answer beat
maths_rules: row r starts after r - 1 full rows of 4 numbers, so column c of row r holds 4(r - 1) + c
124 = 4 x 31, remainder 0: row 31, column 4; 147 = 4 x 36 + 3: row 37, column 3; 201 = 4 x 50 + 1: row 51, column 1
multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 fall in columns 3, 2, 1, 4, 3 and repeat
column 4 holds multiples of 4; even numbers sit in columns 2 and 4; odd numbers in columns 1 and 3
check: row 31, column 4 gives 4 x 30 + 4 = 124; row 51, column 1 gives 4 x 50 + 1 = 201
video_script.design: One idea: the full rows before are counted in fours, then the column is added. Assumes the example of a count with a bracket. The first rows of the grid stay on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Numbers are written in rows of four, in an endless grid.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Row one holds one, two, three and four. Row two holds five, six, seven and eight, and so on.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>Which row and column holds a given number, and what patterns do we see?

narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the formula, the places of three numbers, and the patterns. We work the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: First: row r starts after 4(r − 1) numbers ; column c of row r holds 4(r − 1) + c

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, before row r there are four times the bracket r minus one numbers.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Column c then adds c more. The number in row r and column c is four times the bracket r minus one, plus c.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Column one has c as one, column two has c as two, and so on up to four.

beats.on_screen: Second: 124 = 4 × 31, row 31, column 4 ; 147 = 4 × 36 + 3, row 37, column 3 ; 201 = 4 × 50 + 1, row 51, column 1
narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, divide the number by four. One hundred and twenty four is thirty one fours. Nothing is left, so it is in row thirty one, column four.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>One hundred and forty seven is thirty six fours and three more, so row thirty seven, column three.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Two hundred and one is fifty fours and one more, so row fifty one, column one.

beats.on_screen: Third: multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 ... fall in columns 3, 2, 1, 4, 3 ... then repeat

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, colour the multiples of three: three, six, nine and twelve.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>They sit in columns three, two, one and four. The next multiples fall in columns three, two, one and four again.

<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Odd numbers sit only in columns one and three.
